issues.legal_issue: A holder of land permanently settled after the resumption of an invalid revenue-free grant has rights in the subsoil minerals when the settlement gives the holder the same proprietary rights as a zamindar.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed through predecessors who had held the land under revenue-free religious grants that were found invalid and resumed by the Government.

After resumption, the Government permanently settled the land with the plaintiffs’ predecessors, who held it directly from the Government as proprietors rather than under a subordinate tenure from a zamindar.
The settlement records identified the holders as proprietors of the resumed land under the sovereign.
The defendant’s predecessor and related mining interests extracted coal from beneath the land, and the plaintiffs sued for damages based on their claimed mineral rights.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs’ proprietary rights extended to the subsoil minerals, including the coal beneath the land. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Regulation XIX of 1793, Section IV, treated grantees or possessors of affected land as proprietors with the same right of property as proprietors of estates or dependent taluks, subject to revenue. Regulation VIII of 1793, Section IV, recognized zamindars and other actual proprietors of the soil, and Regulation I of 1793, Section IV, made the settlement permanent. The Court relied on Ranjit Singh v. Kali Dasi Debi for the recognition of zamindars as proprietors of the soil and applied the principle that their rights extend to subsoil minerals. Hari Narayan Singh v. Sri Ram Chakrabarti, Durga Prasad Singh v. Braja Nath Bose, Sashi Bhusan Misra v. Jyoti Prasad Singh Deo, and Raghunath Roy Marwari v. Raja of Jheria concerned subordinate tenure holders and did not govern holders who received settlement directly from the Government.

rule.if: mineral_ownership_dispute and invalid_revenue_free_land_resumed and land_permanently_settled_with_holder and holder_recognized_as_proprietor_under_sovereign

predicates.mineral_ownership_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a holder of land owns minerals beneath it.
predicates.invalid_revenue_free_land_resumed: The Government resumed land after finding the revenue-free grant under which it was held invalid.
predicates.land_permanently_settled_with_holder: The Government permanently settled the resumed land with the holder.
predicates.holder_recognized_as_proprietor_under_so: The settlement treated the holder as a proprietor under the sovereign, rather than as a subordinate tenure holder under a zamindar.

issues.definition: When a mineral-ownership dispute concerns land resumed from an invalid revenue-free grant and permanently settled by the Government with a holder recognized as its proprietor, the holder owns the subsoil minerals.
